data.claim: Two holes: (1) all 34 leaking events are dated <= 2026-10-05, before write-time redaction of every kind (B5deba76d04, 2026-10-08); (2) redact_event_data leaves LOG_VERBATIM fields (url, path, worktree, branch, tags, globs, subject) untouched, so a LAN host in a PR url still leaks today. No test scans the event log.
data.falsifier: A pr.opened event with url=http://<lan ip>/.. written via EventLog.append has no private host in the shard.
data.mechanism: redact_event_data skips k in LOG_VERBATIM_NAMES wholesale; tests/test_repo_is_generic exempts .ddflow/events/.

chunk_findings.detail: The new “knob switches it off” test never exercises the `EventLog` config path. It calls `R.redact_event_data` directly with `lookup_network=False` and compares it to a direct default call, so it would pass even if `ddflow/infra/log.py` ignored `self._lookup_net` and always passed `lookup_network=True`. As written, the actual write-time wiring added by this change is untested for the off setting; a root with `session.redact_lookup_network=false` should leave a URL containing `[REDACTED:ipv4]` untouched, but no such `EventLog.append` is performed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_log_redaction_lookups.py:test_the_knob_switches_it_off

chunk_findings.detail: The helper decides whether to scan an event by string-comparing the raw `ts` value with `EVENT_LOG_CLEAN_FROM`. That comparison is not correct for valid ISO-8601 timestamps. For example, `"2026-10-06T00:00:00.001Z"` is one millisecond after the cutover, but Python compares it as less than `"2026-10-06T00:00:00Z"` because `'.'` < `'Z'`. A new event at that timestamp containing `"http://[REDACTED:ipv4]:80"` would be skipped and `test_no_new_event_names_a_private_network_host` would not flag it, even though it is an event after the clean date.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_repo_is_generic.py:_event_log_leaks

chunk_findings.detail: The event-log leak detector still calls `_private_addresses`, which detects dotted private IPv4 addresses only. The change's requirement is to scan the event log with the same rules as the shared redactor, covering private addresses, hostnames, and keys. An event written after `EVENT_LOG_CLEAN_FROM` whose text field leaks a private hostname or key would produce no hits here, so the regression test passes even if the integration between `EventLog._write` and `redact_event_data` fails for those leak types.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_repo_is_generic.py:_event_log_leaks

chunk_findings.detail: `HOST = "[REDACTED:host]"` is a committed private-host literal in a newly tracked file. The same test asserts this exact host is redacted from `.ddflow/events/*.jsonl` (e.g. in `test_a_lookup_field_carries_no_private_host`), so the project’s network-redaction rules classify `*.home.arpa` as private. Because `tests/test_repo_is_generic.py` scans tracked files with the same address rules, adding this tracked file makes the repository scan fail on its own test source, so the change cannot pass the very leak check it is meant to enforce.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_log_redaction_lookups.py:18

chunk_findings.detail: The scan does not use the shared redactor/network rules; it calls `_private_addresses`, which only recognizes private IPv4 dotted-quad strings. An event written after the cutoff that leaks a private hostname, IPv6 address, or key, e.g. `{"ts": "2026-10-20T00:00:00Z", "data": {"text": "host [REDACTED:host]"}}`, yields `_private_addresses(line) == set()`, so `test_no_new_event_names_a_private_network_host` passes. This misses part of the bug intent that the event log be scanned with the same address rules.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_repo_is_generic.py:_event_log_leaks

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts `not _event_log_leaks()`, but `_event_log_leaks` returns `{}` both when the event log is clean and when `ROOT/.ddflow/events` does not exist or contains no `*.jsonl` shards. In a checkout/CI environment where the event log directory is absent or excluded, the regression silently passes without scanning anything, so a future event-log leak would not be caught.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_repo_is_generic.py:test_no_new_event_names_a_private_network_host
